candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 23 Instead, guidance documents describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be 24 viewed only as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. 25 The use of the word should in Agency guidance documents means that something is suggested or 26 recommended, but not required. 27
candidates.context: This guidance provides recommendations for clinical drug development for drugs intended to treat 17 patients with interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome (IC/BPS). This guidance incorporates 18 advice FDA received at a December 2017 advisory committee meeting 2 on appropriate patient 19 selection criteria and trial design features, including enrollment criteria and acceptable efficacy 20 endpoints for drugs intended to treat IC/BPS. 21 Although this guidance discusses the selection of endpoints for clinical trials, it does not address 29 detailed design considerations for patient-reported outcome (PRO) instruments. Those issues are 30 addressed in the FDA guidance for industry Patient-Reported Outcome Measures: Use in 31

candidates.statement: Current IC/BPS clinical diagnosis criteria encompasses a very heterogeneous patient population 84 who present with a common symptom: pain or discomfort localized to the bladder. Historically, 85 this has resulted in difficulty developing drug products intended for use in a heterogenous patient 86 population. Early clinical trials during drug development should focus on well-defined IC/BPS 87 populations with similar clinical features in addition to pain or discomfort localized to the 88 bladder. This approach may better inform the selection of clinically meaningful efficacy 89 endpoints and outcomes for future studies. 90

candidates.statement: Patients’ experience with IC/BPS symptoms may vary (e.g., symptom type, severity, and 97 duration). It is important to incorporate the patient’s voice during early drug development. 98 Obtaining information from patients can better define the appropriate target population (e.g., 99 IC/BPS patient subpopulations) and identify what matters most to patients regarding their 100 condition to inform endpoint selection. Sponsors should specify and define concepts (e.g., 101 symptoms, functional impacts) early in development that are both relevant and important to 102 patients with IC/BPS. These concepts are more likely to lead to demonstration of clinically 103 meaningful and interpretable changes in later planned clinical trials. Identification of concepts 104 should come from patient input (e.g., conducting patient interviews, identifying literature related 105 to previously conducted patient qualitative studies). The Agency refers sponsors to the following 106 guidances for industry, FDA staff, and other stakeholders for more details about the collection of 107 evidence to inform the patient experience and obtain information from patients, caregivers, and 108 other relevant stakeholders: 109
